data.narrative:
Near Space Labs is a Series B space and aerospace company that has raised $40M+ to date. The valuation analysis considers a comp universe of 5 public-market peers (RKLB, PL, LUNR, ASTS, SATL) and 8 private peers including Cowboy Space Corporation, Aalyria, and Skyryse, though detailed public-comp pricing is not applicable given unavailable revenue data.

Two triangulation methods are applicable. Stage-progression analysis uses the $40M raised proxy as a base and applies a 1.9x Series B step-up multiplier, yielding $76M. Peer-median analysis across four same-sector, same/adjacent-stage private comparables yields a median valuation of $1.6B, with a range from $1.1B (Skyryse, Series C) to $8.0B (Sierra Space, Series C). The peer set spans Series B and Series C positions, introducing stage heterogeneity into the median estimate.

The triangulated range implied by these two methods spans $65M to $1.9B, with a median of $863M. This wide dispersion reflects material tension between stage-progression math ($76M) and peer multiples ($1.6B). Key uncertainties include the revenue profile and unit economics versus comparables—particularly whether Near Space Labs aligns with higher-valuation Series B peers like Cowboy Space Corporation ($2.0B) or lower-valuation Aalyria ($1.3B). Stage-progression alone warrants skepticism given early-stage private data quality. A narrower view emerges in the $400M–$1.3B band if peer stage-matching is weighted more heavily.
